title: OpenCode operating card correction status
summary: This reference explains why the requested source-currency correction cannot yet be applied without inventing information. It identifies the evidence required to complete a correction-only update.
prerequisites: The current resource JSON and its repository-relative target path
The original source records and any replacement source location

sections.title: Can the correction be applied now?
paragraphs: No. The changed cited source, its replacement URL, and the OpenCode claims affected by the change are UNKNOWN. The current resource JSON and exact target filename are also unavailable, so applying an update would require inventing metadata or replacing material that may be unaffected.

This reference is written at the intermediate level. A practitioner should stop before editing and obtain the existing JSON, the three original source records, and evidence identifying the moved or overdue source. If any of those records cannot be obtained, record the correction as blocked rather than guessing.

sections.title: What the inspection established
paragraphs: The inspection reported that the item and all three sources claimed a lastVerified value of 2026-07-26 and that this was future-dated when inspected. The inspection date is UNKNOWN, and no successful source-check date was supplied. Therefore 2026-07-26 cannot be treated as a valid currency signal for the requested correction.

Which cited source changed is UNKNOWN because the original titles and URLs were not supplied. What the change affected is also UNKNOWN because neither the former source content nor replacement content was supplied. If the old and replacement records become available, compare only the claims supported by that source. If the comparison cannot establish an affected claim, leave that claim unchanged and mark the update blocked.

The inspection also challenged provider-neutral classification because the subject is OpenCode. The permitted providers enum contains no OpenCode value, so provider-neutral remains the only schema-permitted classification available for this subject. If the catalogue requires a distinct classification, obtain an approved enum value before changing the field.

A SHA-256 digest cannot reconstruct the resource or source text from which it was calculated. If the baseline cannot be located by its supplied digest, request the exact file from the repository owner instead of attempting to recreate it.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: A complete correction requires the repository-relative target path, the current JSON object, the former source title and HTTPS URL, the replacement HTTPS URL, evidence of the movement or revision, and the claims affected by that source. It also requires a successful check of every retained source and the actual date of each check.

Verify the result by parsing the updated file as one JSON object, confirming that id and slug match the target filename, confirming that exactly three sections remain, and comparing the update against the baseline. The diff should contain only the corrected source record, supported affected claims, valid verification dates, and any provider classification authorized by the schema.

Successful completion also requires every source URL to open directly over HTTPS. If a URL does not resolve, replace it only with a verified first-party location. If no verified replacement exists, do not publish the correction.
